cues.title: The Empty Housing
cues.subtitle: Campaign 1: The Lantern Road  -  Level 1  -  4 Emberfall 1047 AK
cues.text: The Lantern Road runs south from Brindle Cross toward Fort Harrow, one lantern to every mile. A mile out of the village, Lantern Thirty-Seven stands dark for the first time in three hundred years. Last night goblins came up this road. This afternoon four strangers walk down it: a soldier, an archivist, a card player and a priestess, promised free board at the Crooked Kettle if they can bring the light back.
The Lantern Road  -  One Mile South  -  Day
The south road out of Brindle Cross. Four strangers, one mile, and no agreement yet on who walks in front.
Mossfoot. Why's a card player walking an empty road?
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Big Man! You do talk to me. I was starting to think you only spoke to goblins and onions.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Truth is, I once walked the whole width of the Vael for a bet. Roads are where the good stories are.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: That's not an answer.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: It's a story. Better than an answer. Lasts longer.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: 'Brindle Cross, one mile. Fort Harrow, thirty-nine.' It is thirty-eight and a half. Someone carved this in a hurry.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Thirty-nine miles. Two days' march. Less, with nobody arguing.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Past the bend, the birds have stopped singing. The grass around the dark lantern is the colour of old ash.
Listen. No birds past the bend. And the grass has gone grey. In daylight.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Fringe Unlight. Halbrecht's Lantern Theory, the 1002 edition, says it takes days to gather. It has been one night.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Lovely. Let's go and stand in it.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: The Lantern Road  -  The Empty Housing  -  Day
Lantern Thirty-Seven. Its glass is grey and furred with frost, though the afternoon sun is warm on everyone's back.
The Order issues every inspector a housing key. It is in here. Somewhere. Between the almanac and my spare quills.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Professor, may I? It's a catch, not a riddle.
cues.speaker: tamsin

roll.purpose: c1: Work open a frost-stiff Lamplighter housing catch by hand while Ilsevel is still looking for the key, with three peo

cues.text: Tamsin breathes on her fingers, slides a hairpin under the frosted catch, and leans. For a long moment, nothing. Then it gives.
There. Stubborn little thing. And somebody's been in here before me.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: See the scratches round the catch? Fresh. Someone opened this lately, and not with a key.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: You did that in less time than it takes me to find a key. I am writing that down.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Write down that I'm charming.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: I will write down that you are practised.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Ilsevel leans into the open housing, close enough that her breath frosts on the glass.

roll.purpose: c2: Read the inside of an empty lantern housing: tool marks, the cradle clasps, frost patterns. Ilsevel knows lantern-cr

cues.text: The cradle inside is empty. No shards in the grass, no crack in the glass. Whatever burned here was lifted out whole.
It was not broken. It was taken. Lifted out of its cradle like an egg from a nest.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Who did it, or how, this housing will not tell me. I have read every book on lantern-craft in the Hall. None of them covers theft.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Goblins. The goblin said they carry the stones.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Goblins who open a Lamplighter housing without a key. Technically possible. I do not like it.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Oriel lays her palm flat against the iron post. It is cold enough to ache.
Aurelan, keep the light. Keep the road. Keep...
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: She waits for the warmth that has always answered her. It does not come. Oriel takes her hand away.
Oriel?
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: It's cold. That's all. It's only cold.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: The Lantern Road  -  The Trail East  -  Dusk
The sun slides down behind the field. Where the dark trail leaves the road, Brannoc goes down on one knee.

roll.purpose: c3: Read a goblin trail on trampled earth in failing light: how many, how old, carrying what.

cues.text: The earth has been trodden to mud by many feet, over and over. Brannoc reads it three ways and believes none of them.
Goblins. Some. Last night, or last week. Can't tell.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Ground's been walked to soup. Could be four. Could be forty.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Forty. Lovely. My favourite number of goblins is none.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: It will be fully dark within the hour. I would like that noted before anyone decides anything.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: And goblins like the dark. Noted twice.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: That's where they went.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Then that's where the light went too. Brannoc, in front?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Single file. Behind me.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Behind them, the road still holds the last of the light. Ahead, the Thornpike Woods are already night.
Somebody starts to hum a hymn, very quietly and not very well.
Sunshine. Are you singing?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Only when I'm nervous. Keep walking.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Next time: Night falls in the Thornpike Woods.
